chapters.title: Combat and Feel
chapters.description: Action games I study for hit weight, readable enemies, timing windows and the camera that holds a fight together.

chapters.title: Worlds and Traversal
chapters.description: Worlds that taught me how pacing, landmarks and movement make a place worth exploring.

chapters.title: Characters and Story
chapters.description: Games where character, routine and pacing changed my standard for emotional payoff.

chapters.title: Loops and Retention
chapters.description: Repeatable loops, short sessions and clear goals that keep players coming back, including the casual and puzzle games closest to my studio work.

chapters.title: Systems and Economy
chapters.description: Strategy and RPG systems I return to for tradeoffs, economy tension and choices that compound.

chapters.title: Lessons From Friction
chapters.description: Games that did not fully land for me, and the questions they left about player trust, expectation and scope.

chapters.title: Memory Shelf
chapters.description: Other games that shaped my taste along the way, from first Pokemon runs to long Dynasty Warriors nights.

games.title: Red Dead Redemption 2
games.reflection: Slow travel and small interruptions on the road make the frontier feel lived in. It taught me that pacing between moments matters as much as the moments themselves.

games.title: Elden Ring
games.reflection: It trusts players to read danger and reward from the landscape, with almost no markers. I use it to check whether a space explains itself.

games.title: Witcher 3
games.reflection: Side quests matter because they grow out of local problems and real characters. A standard for content that feels written for its place.

games.title: Persona 5 Royal
games.reflection: Interface, calendar, music and character arcs all push the same fantasy. My reference for style that does gameplay work instead of decorating it.

games.title: Persona 3 Reload
games.reflection: A limited calendar turns ordinary days into choices with weight. I keep it in mind when a schedule or timer needs to carry emotion.

games.title: L.A. Noire
games.reflection: A memorable case of performance capture, detective fantasy, and the tension between authored drama and player interpretation.

games.title: Plants vs. Zombies GOTY Edition
games.reflection: Clear lanes, one new idea per level and rewards on time, so anyone can start. I used the same idea when pacing difficulty across a puzzle level set.

games.title: God of War 4
games.reflection: A close camera makes every hit feel heavy, but only because enemy attacks are telegraphed for that framing. When I design camera and combat together, I start from what the player must see before a hit lands.

games.title: Ninja Gaiden 4
games.reflection: Fast and punishing, yet fair, because every enemy shows its intent before it strikes. The lesson I take: raise speed only as far as the tells stay readable.

games.title: The First Berserker: Khazan
games.reflection: Heavy attacks and tight timing windows reward staying aggressive instead of waiting. I use it as a reference for making the risky choice the fun one.

games.title: Nine Sols
games.reflection: Parry rhythm is the whole fight: bosses teach a pattern, then remix it. A clean model for escalating an encounter without adding new rules.

games.title: Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty
games.reflection: Deflection ties defence to offence, and morale makes every fight a small risk-reward choice. Useful when I want one system to carry both safety and greed.

games.title: Stellar Blade
games.reflection: Big, cinematic animations that still answer the button instantly. A reminder that spectacle must never cost responsiveness.

games.title: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim
games.reflection: Landmarks pull the player off the path every few minutes. I borrow that rhythm of curiosity when spacing content in a level.

games.title: Marvel's Spider-Man 2
games.reflection: Moving through the city is the fun before any mission starts. Proof that traversal alone can carry the fantasy.

games.title: Assassin's Creed Black Flag
games.reflection: Sailing became the part people remember, more than the main loop. A lesson in how a side system can become a game's identity.

games.title: The Last of Us Part I
games.imageAlt: The Last of Us Part I artwork
games.reflection: Restraint everywhere: quiet rooms, small details, trust that breaks slowly. It shows how environment and pacing can tell the story without a cutscene.

games.title: NieR:Automata
games.reflection: Repeating the story from another view changes what it means. A reminder that mechanics and structure can carry a theme, not just the script.

games.title: Yakuza: Like a Dragon
games.reflection: Absurd side stories that still feel sincere, because the party has clear personalities. Proof that tone can swing widely if characters stay consistent.

games.title: God of War Ragnarok
games.reflection: Companion dialogue during play builds the relationship more than the cutscenes. Useful when content has to carry character between big beats.

games.title: Hades 2
games.reflection: Every failed run moves the story forward, so repetition never feels wasted. A model for giving players a reason to start one more run.

games.title: Dead Cells
games.reflection: Instant restarts and permanent unlocks take the sting out of dying without removing tension. I use it to judge how much a failure should cost.

games.title: Stardew Valley
games.reflection: Daily choices, comfort and long-term goals support each other instead of competing. A reference for a loop that lasts hundreds of hours.

games.title: Goods Sort Puzzle
games.reflection: Short sessions, a tactile sort and a screen that visibly clears. The same feeling I designed for in GoodSort's shelf layouts.

games.title: Screw Jam
games.reflection: Clear constraints and fast restarts keep the puzzle energy high. A direct reference for my level design work on Screw.

games.title: Civilization VI
games.reflection: Small decisions compound over hundreds of turns, and every tradeoff is visible. I aimed for the same readable economy in Lunarfall's resource sheet.

games.title: Total War: Three Kingdoms
games.reflection: Character relationships drive the campaign map, so loyalty and ambition become strategy. A lesson in tying systems to people.

games.title: Total War: Warhammer
games.reflection: Factions play differently, and the rules themselves express each faction's identity. My reference for asymmetric design.

games.title: Teamfight Tactics
games.reflection: Gold, levels and rerolls create constant economy tension, and pivots stay readable. Useful when I balance a resource players must spend under pressure.

games.title: Baldur's Gate 3
games.reflection: Almost any plan is allowed and the world reacts to it. A benchmark for systems that reward creative problem solving.

games.title: Divinity: Original Sin 2
games.reflection: Elemental surfaces turn the battlefield into a toolbox. A reminder that a few systemic rules can create many solutions.

games.title: Dynasty Warriors 9
games.reflection: Going open world diluted what fans loved about the series. A lesson in protecting the core before changing the formula.

games.title: Watch Dogs
games.reflection: The promise was bigger than the interactions in the city. A reminder that marketing sets the bar the systems must meet.

games.title: Cyberpunk 2077 (PS4/XOne)
games.reflection: On old consoles, broken immersion overshadowed a strong world. Launch conditions can define how a game is remembered.

games.title: Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy DE
games.imageAlt: Grand Theft Auto The Trilogy Definitive Edition artwork
games.reflection: New visuals lost the original look and feel. Proof that a remaster has to protect identity, not just raise resolution.

games.title: Assassin's Creed Unity
games.reflection: Huge crowds and parkour impressed, but unreliable feedback wore down trust. Ambition only works when the basics feel dependable.

games.title: Batman: Arkham Knight
games.reflection: Crowd combat stays readable through one clear signal: the counter prompt. When a fight gets busy, I look for the single cue that tells the player what to do next.

games.title: Temple Run
games.reflection: One input, instant failure feedback and a strong one-more-run pull. The simplest proof that clarity drives retention.

games.title: Far Cry Primal
games.reflection: A useful world reference for survival dressing, environmental readability, and theme carrying familiar systems.

games.title: Assassin's Creed Odyssey
games.reflection: A large-scale reference for destination density, historical fantasy, and the risk of too much map pressure.

games.title: Ori and the Blind Forest
games.imageAlt: Ori and the Blind Forest artwork
games.reflection: A compact reminder that movement, color, and music can make a world feel emotionally precise.

games.title: Sleeping Dogs
games.reflection: A city memory built from martial arts fantasy, street texture, and compact open-world pacing.

games.title: Mafia II
games.reflection: A memory of authored crime drama where city atmosphere supports a focused, linear story.

games.title: Valiant Hearts
games.reflection: A compact memory of how illustration, puzzle pacing, and historical tone can carry emotion without mechanical complexity.

games.title: Persona 4 Golden
games.reflection: A reference for social routine, small-town mystery, and using calendar pressure to build attachment.

games.title: Heavy Rain
games.reflection: A useful case for authored tension, player performance, and how interaction can heighten awkward drama.

games.title: Assassin's Creed III
games.reflection: A story memory where ambition, historical framing, and uneven pacing still left useful lessons.

games.title: Castlevania: Lords of Shadow
games.reflection: A gothic action memory where mood, scale, and boss framing did a lot of the emotional work.

games.title: Naruto Shippuden: Ultimate Ninja Storm 4
games.imageAlt: Naruto Shippuden Ultimate Ninja Storm 4 artwork
games.reflection: A useful fan-service reference for cinematic combat readability and adapting anime spectacle into inputs.

games.title: Left 4 Dead 2
games.reflection: A clean multiplayer loop reference for pressure pacing, readable roles, and improvisation inside simple rules.

games.title: One Piece: Pirate Warriors 4
games.reflection: A comfort-loop example where spectacle, simple inputs, and character collection carry the session rhythm.

games.title: Dead Island
games.reflection: A messy but memorable loot-and-survival loop where co-op friction became part of the memory.

games.title: Kingdom Come: Deliverance
games.reflection: A reference for grounded role-play, where friction becomes identity because progression asks the player to inhabit weakness first.

games.title: Pokemon Emerald
games.reflection: A milestone memory for collection, party identity, and learning how small choices build ownership.

games.title: Pokemon Black and White
games.reflection: A nostalgia anchor for creature design, journey structure, and the comfort of clear progression.

games.title: Dynasty Warriors 8
games.reflection: A milestone in power-fantasy loops where repetition, roster breadth, and spectacle were the appeal.

games.title: Dynasty Warriors 7
games.reflection: A memory shelf game for simple spectacle, historical melodrama, and repeated comfort play.

games.title: Far Cry 3
games.reflection: A milestone open-world memory for outpost loops, villain presence, and improvisational chaos.

games.title: Assassin's Creed II
games.reflection: A milestone memory for movement fantasy, historical spaces, and how a strong protagonist can anchor a long journey.

games.title: League of Legends
games.reflection: A long-term memory of mastery pressure, team dynamics, and how live games become social habits.

games.title: Ni no Kuni II: Revenant Kingdom
games.imageAlt: Ni no Kuni II: Revenant Kingdom artwork
games.reflection: A bright reference for fairy-tale world tone, soft stakes, and kingdom-scale progression.

games.title: Prototype
games.reflection: A useful memory of readable chaos, mobility, and letting the player feel dangerous quickly.

games.title: Dave the Diver
games.reflection: A compact example of place identity built through routines, surprises, and gentle escalation.

games.title: Uncharted: Legacy of Thieves Collection
games.imageAlt: Uncharted: Legacy of Thieves Collection artwork
games.reflection: A polished reminder that spectacle works best when geography, pacing, and performance align.

games.title: Dispatch
games.reflection: A reminder that workplace rhythm and choice pressure can frame character drama without huge scale.

games.title: The Wolf Among Us
games.reflection: A noir structure lesson in mood, dialogue tension, and mystery as forward motion.

games.title: To the Moon
games.reflection: Proof that limited mechanics can still deliver a memorable emotional arc when the premise is clear.

games.title: Sherlock Holmes: The Devil's Daughter
games.imageAlt: Sherlock Holmes: The Devil's Daughter artwork
games.reflection: A case-study memory for investigation flow, clue framing, and uneven but useful deduction fantasy.

games.title: Sherlock Holmes: Crimes & Punishments
games.reflection: A clearer reference for branching conclusions and making interpretation feel like play.

games.title: Plants vs. Zombies 2
games.reflection: A casual strategy loop that keeps variation readable even when the content structure expands.

games.title: It Takes Two
games.reflection: A cooperative pacing reference where every chapter refreshes interaction before the loop gets stale.

games.title: Split Fiction
games.reflection: A modern co-op reminder that constant mechanical remixing can be the main spectacle.

games.title: Stick War: Legacy
games.reflection: A small-screen strategy loop with clear unit identity, simple pressure, and quick readability.

games.title: Where's My Water?
games.reflection: A clean physics puzzle memory where the player understands the goal before touching the screen.

games.title: Pokemon Unite
games.reflection: A streamlined team objective loop that compresses MOBA pressure into approachable match length.

games.title: Have a Nice Death
games.reflection: A roguelite memory for snappy combat, office-themed identity, and repeat-run texture.

games.title: Dead by Daylight
games.reflection: An asymmetric loop lesson in tension, role fantasy, and player-made drama.

games.title: Don't Starve
games.reflection: A survival loop where discovery, scarcity, and consequence make each routine feel fragile.

games.title: DNF Duel
games.reflection: A fighting-game systems reference where exaggerated kits make matchup identity easy to read.

games.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
games.reflection: A turn-based reference where timing, style, and presentation make familiar inputs feel sharp again.

games.title: No Rest for the Wicked
games.imageAlt: No Rest for the Wicked artwork
games.reflection: A systems memory for action-RPG weight, resource pressure, and build decisions under friction.

games.title: The Incredible Adventures of Van Helsing
games.imageAlt: The Incredible Adventures of Van Helsing artwork
games.reflection: A loot-action reference for class fantasy, companion texture, and compact progression hooks.

games.title: Pokemon Scarlet and Violet
games.reflection: A milestone memory for open-ended Pokemon structure, collection flow, and uneven ambition.

games.title: Pokemon Omega Ruby
games.reflection: A remake memory tied to comfort, region identity, and the familiar rhythm of team building.

games.title: Dynasty Warriors 7: Xtreme Legends
games.reflection: A musou expansion memory for spectacle density, roster attachment, and simple power fantasy.

games.title: Dynasty Warriors: Origins
games.reflection: A newer milestone in a long-running comfort series, useful for comparing scale and feel across eras.

games.title: Naruto Mobile
games.reflection: A mobile anime-action memory where familiarity, collection, and bursty combat carry retention.

games.title: Jump Force
games.reflection: A crossover memory that is more about dream roster energy than perfect competitive structure.

games.title: Naruto: Ultimate Ninja Storm Series
games.imageAlt: Naruto: Ultimate Ninja Storm Series artwork
games.reflection: A franchise-level memory for cinematic anime combat, spectacle timing, and fan-service pacing.
